# QA Analysis: Password Reset Using Registered Email

## Scope and assumptions

**Requirement:** A user can reset their password using their registered email address.

The following items are not defined by the requirement and should be confirmed with Product/Engineering:

- Whether reset begins from a “Forgot password?” link.
- Whether the email is case-insensitive.
- Whether unregistered emails receive the same response as registered emails.
- Token expiration duration and whether tokens are single-use.
- Password complexity rules.
- Whether existing sessions are invalidated after reset.
- Whether the user is automatically logged in after reset.
- Email delivery provider and expected delivery time.
- Rate-limiting and account-lockout behavior.
- Whether reset links can be used more than once.

The scenarios below identify these as assumptions where applicable.

---

# 1. Positive test scenarios

| ID | Scenario | Expected result | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| PWR-001 | Registered user submits a valid registered email | Password reset process starts successfully and an appropriate confirmation is shown | High |
| PWR-002 | User receives password reset email for a registered account | Email is delivered to the registered email address and contains a valid reset link or instructions | High |
| PWR-003 | User opens a valid reset link | Password reset page is displayed | High |
| PWR-004 | User submits a valid new password and confirmation password | Password is updated successfully | High |
| PWR-005 | User logs in using the new password | Login succeeds with the new password | High |
| PWR-006 | User cannot log in with the previous password after reset | Previous password is rejected, assuming old passwords are invalidated | High |
| PWR-007 | User submits an email with leading/trailing whitespace | Email is handled according to the defined normalization rules; typically whitespace is trimmed | Medium |
| PWR-008 | User submits a valid email using different letter casing | Request succeeds if email matching is case-insensitive, as commonly expected | Medium |
| PWR-009 | User clicks the reset link from a supported browser or device | Reset page opens and token remains valid | Medium |
| PWR-010 | User resets password with the minimum valid password | Password is accepted | High |
| PWR-011 | User resets password with a password longer than the minimum | Password is accepted if within the configured maximum length | Medium |
| PWR-012 | User enters matching new password and confirmation values | Form can be submitted successfully | High |
| PWR-013 | User requests reset more than once and uses the latest valid link | Behavior matches the product rule; commonly, the latest token remains valid | Medium |
| PWR-014 | User completes reset after navigating away and returning to the reset page | Valid token continues to work, if tokens are not session-bound | Low |
| PWR-015 | Password reset is completed through the supported API, if an API exists | API returns the documented success response and updates the password | High |

---

# 2. Negative test scenarios

| ID | Scenario | Expected result | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| NWR-001 | User submits an unregistered email | A safe response is shown; the system should not reveal whether the account exists | High |
| NWR-002 | User submits an empty email | Required-field validation is shown and no request is sent | High |
| NWR-003 | User submits an invalid email format | Format validation is shown and no reset request is processed | High |
| NWR-004 | User submits whitespace-only input | Input is rejected as empty or invalid | Medium |
| NWR-005 | User opens a malformed reset URL | Reset is rejected and an appropriate error is shown | High |
| NWR-006 | User opens a reset URL with a missing token | Reset page is not usable and an error is shown | High |
| NWR-007 | User opens an expired reset link | Reset is rejected and the user is instructed to request a new link | High |
| NWR-008 | User opens an already-used reset link | Reset is rejected if tokens are single-use | High |
| NWR-009 | User tampers with the reset token | Reset is rejected | High |
| NWR-010 | User submits a new password that does not meet complexity requirements | Validation is shown and password is not changed | High |
| NWR-011 | New password and confirmation password do not match | Validation is shown and password is not changed | High |
| NWR-012 | New password is empty | Required-field validation is shown | High |
| NWR-013 | Confirmation password is empty | Required-field validation is shown | High |
| NWR-014 | New password exceeds the configured maximum length | Validation is shown, if a maximum exists | Medium |
| NWR-015 | New password is the same as the old password | Behavior follows the defined password reuse rule; reject if reuse is prohibited | Medium |
| NWR-016 | User submits multiple reset requests rapidly | Requests are rate-limited or handled according to the security policy | High |
| NWR-017 | User tries to reset a disabled, locked, or deleted account | Reset is rejected or handled according to the account lifecycle rules | High |
| NWR-018 | Email delivery fails | User receives a safe, actionable response; system records the failure without exposing sensitive details | Medium |
| NWR-019 | User attempts to use the reset endpoint without a valid CSRF protection mechanism, where applicable | Request is rejected | High |
| NWR-020 | User enters script or HTML in the email or password fields | Input is safely handled; no script executes or unsafe content is rendered | High |
| NWR-021 | User uses an invalid token after successfully changing the password | Token cannot be reused | High |
| NWR-022 | User requests reset for an email containing SQL/script injection characters | Input is safely validated or rejected; no server-side injection occurs | High |

---

# 3. Edge cases

| ID | Edge case | Expected result | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| EC-001 | Email address contains uppercase characters | Matching follows the documented email normalization behavior | Medium |
| EC-002 | Email address contains leading/trailing spaces | Spaces are trimmed or input is rejected consistently | Medium |
| EC-003 | Email is at the maximum supported length | Accepted if valid and within limits | Medium |
| EC-004 | Email exceeds the maximum supported length | Rejected safely without server error | Medium |
| EC-005 | Internationalized email address | Supported or rejected consistently according to system capabilities | Low |
| EC-006 | Password contains spaces | Accepted or rejected according to password policy | Medium |
| EC-007 | Password contains Unicode characters or emoji | Behavior follows the documented password policy | Low |
| EC-008 | Password contains special characters | Accepted if allowed by the password policy | Medium |
| EC-009 | Password is exactly at the minimum length | Accepted if all other rules pass | High |
| EC-010 | Password is one character below the minimum | Rejected | High |
| EC-011 | Password is exactly at the maximum length | Accepted if a maximum exists | Medium |
| EC-012 | Password exceeds the maximum length by one character | Rejected or safely handled | Medium |
| EC-013 | Reset link is opened in multiple browser tabs | Token behavior is consistent and secure | Medium |
| EC-014 | Reset link is opened after the token expiration boundary | Token is rejected | High |
| EC-015 | User submits the reset form twice | Only one valid password update occurs; duplicate submission is handled safely | High |
| EC-016 | Network disconnects during reset submission | User receives a recoverable error and system does not leave an ambiguous unsafe state | Medium |
| EC-017 | Email arrives after the user requests another reset | Token precedence and validity follow the defined rule | Medium |
| EC-018 | Reset link is copied into another browser or device | Behavior follows the token/session security policy | Medium |
| EC-019 | User clicks browser Back after reset | Previously submitted reset form or token cannot be reused | High |
| EC-020 | Concurrent password-reset requests are made for the same account | Token and password update behavior remain secure and deterministic | High |

---

# 4. Test data suggestions

## Account data

| Data set | Example | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Active registered account | `qa.reset.user@example.test` | Standard positive testing |
| Unregistered email | `not.registered@example.test` | Account enumeration and validation |
| Disabled account | `disabled.user@example.test` | Account lifecycle handling |
| Locked account | `locked.user@example.test` | Security behavior |
| Mixed-case registered email | `Qa.Reset.User@Example.Test` | Case normalization |
| Email with surrounding spaces | ` qa.reset.user@example.test ` | Input normalization |
| Maximum-length valid email | Valid email at supported boundary | Boundary testing |
| Invalid email formats | `user`, `user@`, `@example.test`, `user@@example.test` | Format validation |
| Script-like input | `<script>alert(1)</script>` | Input security |
| SQL-like input | `' OR '1'='1` | Injection handling |

Use a test domain such as `example.test` rather than real user addresses.

## Password data

| Data set | Example | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Valid minimum-length password | Based on configured policy | Boundary testing |
| Valid complex password | `Qa!Reset2025#Valid` | Standard positive test |
| Too-short password | Below minimum length | Validation |
| Missing uppercase | Policy-dependent | Complexity validation |
| Missing lowercase | Policy-dependent | Complexity validation |
| Missing number | Policy-dependent | Complexity validation |
| Missing special character | Policy-dependent | Complexity validation |
| Password mismatch | `Qa!Reset2025#One` / `Qa!Reset2025#Two` | Confirmation validation |
| Existing password | Previously stored password | Password reuse behavior |
| Maximum-length password | At configured maximum | Boundary testing |
| Overlong password | One or more characters above maximum | Boundary/security testing |
| Unicode password | `Pässwørd🔐!2025` | Encoding support |
| Password containing spaces | `Qa Reset 2025!` | Policy behavior |

## Token data

Where test environments permit token control, prepare:

- Valid unused token
- Expired token
- Already-used token
- Invalid random token
- Tampered token
- Missing token
- Token with invalid characters
- Two tokens generated for the same account
- Token at exactly the expiration boundary

---

# 5. Key security and usability checks

These should be included even though they are not fully specified in the requirement:

- The response for registered and unregistered emails should ideally be indistinguishable to prevent account enumeration.
- Reset tokens should be cryptographically secure, time-limited, and single-use.
- Tokens should not appear in application logs, analytics, or error messages.
- Passwords must never be displayed or logged in plain text.
- Reset links should use HTTPS.
- Reset endpoints should have rate limiting and abuse protection.
- The reset form should not expose account details.
- The new password should be stored securely using an approved password-hashing mechanism.
- The reset email should not include the password.
- Existing sessions should be invalidated if that is the security requirement.
- The confirmation message should be usable with screen readers and keyboard navigation.
- The workflow should work on supported desktop and mobile browsers.

---

# 7. Playwright automation suggestions using Python

## Recommended test structure

Separate tests into:

1. **UI tests**
   - Reset page navigation
   - Field validation
   - Confirmation behavior
   - Reset form interaction

2. **API/service tests**
   - Reset request and completion endpoints
   - Token behavior
   - Rate limiting
   - Security responses

3. **Email integration tests**
   - Use a sandbox mailbox or email interception tool.
   - Avoid relying on real external email delivery in every test.

4. **End-to-end tests**
   - Request reset
   - Retrieve the email
   - Extract the reset link
   - Complete the password reset
   - Log in using the new password

## Example Playwright page-object model

```python
# pages/password_reset_page.py
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


class PasswordResetPage:
    def __init__(self, page: Page):
        self.page = page
        self.email_input = page.get_by_label("Email")
        self.request_button = page.get_by_role(
            "button", name="Reset password"
        )

    def open(self, base_url: str):
        self.page.goto(f"{base_url}/forgot-password")

    def request_reset(self, email: str):
        self.email_input.fill(email)
        self.request_button.click()

    def expect_confirmation(self):
        expect(
            self.page.get_by_text(
                "If an account exists, a reset email has been sent"
            )
        ).to_be_visible()
```

The exact URL, labels, button names, and messages above are examples and must be replaced with the actual application values.

## Example UI tests

import pytest
from playwright.sync_api import expect

from pages.password_reset_page import PasswordResetPage

    reset_page.request_reset(registered_user_email)

## Email retrieval approach

The email should be retrieved through a test-only mechanism such as:

- Mailpit or MailHog
- Mailtrap
- An email provider sandbox API
- A test application endpoint exposing email messages
- A mocked email service

Example using a hypothetical email API:

```python
import re
import requests


def get_reset_link(email_api_url: str, recipient: str) -> str:
    response = requests.get(
        email_api_url,
        params={"recipient": recipient},
        timeout=10,
    )
    response.raise_for_status()

    message = response.json()["latest_message"]
    body = message["body"]

    match = re.search(r"https://[^/\s]+/reset-password\?token=[^"\s]+", body)
    assert match, "Password reset link was not found in the email"

    return match.group(0)
```

This example is intentionally generic. The email API and URL pattern must match the test environment.

## End-to-end example

```python
import pytest


@pytest.mark.e2e
def test_complete_password_reset_flow(
    page, base_url, registered_user_email, email_api_url
):
    reset_page = PasswordResetPage(page)

    reset_page.open(base_url)
    reset_page.request_reset(registered_user_email)
    reset_page.expect_confirmation()

    reset_link = get_reset_link(
        email_api_url=email_api_url,
        recipient=registered_user_email,
    )

    page.goto(reset_link)
    page.get_by_label("New password").fill("Qa!Reset2025#New")
    page.get_by_label("Confirm password").fill("Qa!Reset2025#New")
    page.get_by_role("button", name="Save password").click()

    page.get_by_label("Email").fill(registered_user_email)
    page.get_by_label("Password").fill("Qa!Reset2025#New")
    page.get_by_role("button", name="Sign in").click()

    # Replace with an application-specific authenticated-state assertion.
    assert "/dashboard" in page.url
```

## Useful Playwright practices

- Prefer accessible locators such as `get_by_role()` and `get_by_label()`.
- Avoid brittle CSS selectors and text tied to styling.
- Use isolated users for each test to avoid password and token interference.
- Generate unique test accounts where reset state persists.
- Do not hard-code real credentials or tokens in source control.
- Use API setup for account creation and cleanup when available.
- Capture screenshots and traces only on failure.
- Use polling for email retrieval instead of fixed sleeps.
- Verify the reset token cannot be reused.
- Verify the old password no longer works if that behavior is required.
- Run browser tests across supported browsers and mobile viewports.
- Add accessibility checks for form labels, error messages, focus behavior, and keyboard navigation.

---

# Suggested priority focus

## High priority

- Registered email can request reset.
- Reset email is sent.
- Valid link allows password reset.
- New password can be used for login.
- Invalid, expired, tampered, and reused tokens are rejected.
- Password and confirmation validation works.
- Unregistered email does not expose account existence.
- Rate limiting and injection protection are in place.

## Medium priority

- Email normalization.
- Password boundary values.
- Multiple reset requests.
- Network and email delivery failures.
- Cross-browser and cross-device reset behavior.

## Low priority

- Internationalized email addresses.
- Unicode password behavior, unless explicitly supported.
- Rare navigation and tab scenarios.
- Detailed visual formatting of reset emails.
